title: Career Roadmap · Junior Data Analyst
summary: A Junior Data Analyst collects, cleans, organizes, analyzes, and visualizes data to help organizations make informed decisions. The role combines analytical thinking, statistics, spreadsheets, SQL, dashboards, and basic programming.

blocks.text: A Junior Data Analyst collects, cleans, organizes, analyzes, and visualizes data to help organizations make informed decisions. The role combines analytical thinking, statistics, spreadsheets, SQL, dashboards, and basic programming.

Junior Data Analysts work across industries such as information technology, finance, healthcare, retail, education, logistics, manufacturing, and e-commerce. With an AI Applications specialization, students can also learn how to use AI tools to accelerate data preparation, explore datasets, generate insights, and automate routine reporting.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Collect data from spreadsheets, databases, applications, and business systems.
Clean datasets by handling missing values, duplicates, inconsistent formats, and errors.
Write SQL queries to retrieve, filter, join, and summarize data.
Analyze trends, patterns, and business performance indicators.
Build dashboards and reports using Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.
Use Python libraries for data manipulation and exploratory analysis.
Prepare recurring reports and communicate findings to stakeholders.
Validate data quality and investigate unexpected results.
Support business teams with ad hoc analysis.
Use AI-assisted tools responsibly to support coding, documentation, and analysis.

blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt it to the institution's actual semester structure.
Year 1
Foundation
Build numerical, spreadsheet, and data fundamentals

items.text: Learn descriptive statistics, percentages, ratios, averages, variance, and standard deviation.
Master Excel or Google Sheets, including formulas, sorting, filtering, conditional formatting, and pivot tables.
Understand data types, structured data, tables, rows, columns, and data quality.

blocks.label: Learn basic SQL
blocks.text: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, and aggregate functions.

items.text: Study basic charts and principles of data visualization.
Learn introductory Python syntax, variables, loops, functions, and data structures.
Understand business metrics such as revenue, profit, conversion rate, retention, and growth.
Practise explaining numerical findings in clear, non-technical language.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Analyze a spreadsheet dataset and produce a summary report with charts and actionable observations.
Year 2
Analysis
Develop SQL, Python, and dashboard skills

items.text: Learn SQL joins, subqueries, common table expressions, and introductory window functions.
Use Python with pandas and NumPy for data cleaning and transformation.
Practise exploratory data analysis, outlier detection, and missing-value treatment.
Learn Power BI or Tableau, including data models, filters, measures, and interactive dashboards.
Understand relational databases, primary keys, foreign keys, and normalization basics.
Study probability, sampling, correlation, and introductory hypothesis testing.
Learn how to define KPIs and translate business questions into analytical tasks.
Explore AI-assisted coding and analysis, validating all generated queries and conclusions.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Complete a project that uses SQL or Python to analyze a dataset and a BI tool to present the results.
Year 3
Job readiness
Build an industry-ready portfolio

items.text: Complete an internship in data analytics, business intelligence, or reporting.
Develop end-to-end projects involving data collection, cleaning, analysis, visualization, and recommendations.
Practise writing reusable SQL queries and documenting assumptions.
Build polished Power BI dashboards with meaningful measures and filters.
Learn basic Git and project documentation.
Study data privacy, access controls, responsible AI use, and data governance.
Practise case studies, SQL interview questions, and business problem-solving.
Create a portfolio containing dashboards, notebooks, SQL scripts, and concise project reports.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Present two or three well-documented projects and explain the business problem, methodology, findings, and limitations of each.

Deliverables:

items.text: Define a business problem and analytical questions.
Obtain a public or appropriately authorized dataset.
Inspect and clean the data using Excel, SQL, or Python.
Calculate key performance indicators.
Analyze trends, segments, and exceptions.
Build a Power BI dashboard.
Summarize findings and practical recommendations.
Document assumptions, data limitations, and validation checks.

AI can help generate code and hypotheses, but the analyst remains responsible for validating calculations, understanding context, and communicating uncertainty.
By the end of the B.Voc programme, a job-ready student should aim to have:

items.text: Practical proficiency in Excel, SQL, and a BI tool.
Working knowledge of Python and pandas.
A solid understanding of descriptive statistics and basic inference.
Two or three complete analytics projects.
At least one interactive dashboard and one SQL-focused project.
Experience cleaning, validating, and documenting datasets.
At least one relevant internship or supervised industry assignment.
A portfolio containing code, dashboards, explanations, and project limitations.
The ability to answer business questions using data rather than simply producing charts.
Awareness of data privacy, responsible AI use, and confidentiality.

blocks.label: Recommended first career target
blocks.text: Junior Data Analyst.

blocks.label: Best initial strategy
blocks.text: Focus on Excel, SQL, Power BI, and statistics, then strengthen the profile with Python and applied business projects.

blocks.label: Most valuable differentiator
blocks.text: The ability to turn imperfect data into reliable analysis, explain what the numbers mean, and recommend a practical next step.

blocks.label: Long-term opportunity
blocks.text: Progress into business intelligence, product analytics, marketing analytics, data quality, analytics leadership, or other data-focused roles.
